migrations.summary: jsdom ^30.1.2 is newer than the tested ^30.1.1
migrations.instructions: Meridian is tested against jsdom ^30.1.1; your ^30.1.2 is newer and was left as it is. Run the project's gate and build with it, and read the jsdom release notes for breaking changes before relying on it.

migrations.summary: The product says what an address a person may not open draws: `refusal` in `src/app.config.ts`.
migrations.instructions: Read "Navigation: `src/app.config.ts`" in references/customize.md. Add `export const refusal: 'explain' | 'absent' = 'explain';` to `src/app.config.ts`, beside `facts`: `explain` keeps the no-access page a refused page draws today, and `absent` answers as an address that names nothing. A project that keeps the sample's access seam brings `src/data/access.ts` and `src/data/refusal.ts` over from the release (`gate` reads `refusal`, with `gatedMetadata` and `withheldEntries` beside it, and `gatedLoading` reads it alone), titles each gated page with `export function generateMetadata() { return gatedMetadata('<feature>', { title: '<its title>' }); }` in place of a static `metadata`, passes its loading state's `name` and `title` through `gatedLoading`, and adds `refusal,` to the config object of `scripts/verify.config.ts`, imported from `../src/app.config.ts`, so `verify --as` expects the page the product chose.

migrations.summary: A file of the team's imports an export the release removed from a managed module: `deviations`, `largest`, `runs` or `weekendRatio` from `src/lib/insight.ts`, or `queryInput` from `src/lib/collection.ts`.
migrations.instructions: The update brought `src/lib/insight.ts` and `src/lib/collection.ts` without them, so each file listed here fails the type check. A file of the sample's comes over from the release: the Overview context is Home's, `src/views/home-context.ts` (see `sample-pages-renamed`); the assistant reads through `view_<name>` and `explore_<view>` and has no `query_<name>` tools, so bring `src/lib/assistant/tools.ts` and `src/lib/assistant/respond.ts` over and pass `readable`, every collection the person may read, from the assistant route to `respond` beside `collections` (read "Prepared queries" in references/agents.md); and a shipped test that imports one, such as `tests/shared-context.test.tsx` or `tests/collection.test.ts`, comes over as the release has it. A file of your own that still needs one of the functions writes it in that file, from its 0.15.0 source.

migrations.summary: Every view tool names the page it renders and its prepared query: `page` and `explore` on `defineViewTool`.
migrations.instructions: Read "Prepared queries" in references/agents.md. Add to each `defineViewTool` call in the files listed here `page`, the console route of the page the view renders (a rail destination's `href` in `nav`, or a detail page's route with its segment, such as `/customers/[id]`), and `explore`, its prepared query (`PreparedQuery` in `src/lib/explore.ts`), declared beside the view as the sample's are in `src/views/<view>-explore.ts`. `ViewTool` in `src/lib/shared-context.ts` requires both, so a tool without them fails the type check. A project that kept the sample's view tools brings `src/views/tools.ts` and the `src/views/*-explore.ts` files over from the release. Once a tool names its page, the gate asks that page's specification what the agent does there (`agent-does-here-section`).

migrations.summary: The specification of a page a view tool renders says what the agent does there.
migrations.instructions: Read "Prepared queries" in references/agents.md. Under `## Agents` in the README.md of each page a view tool's `page` names, add `### What the agent does here`: a line `Protagonist: <the card's name>.`, then at least three questions a person on the page asks that its context does not answer alone, each `- "<question>" — <what the prepared query is asked>`, and mark that card on the page with `data-protagonist="<name>"`. `scripts/check.ts` fails the gate on such a page without the part. While a view tool in `src/views/tools.ts` names no page yet (`view-tool-page-explore`), every console page specification without the part is listed: one that no tool comes to name needs nothing.

migrations.summary: The project holds the sample's pages and views under their 0.15.0 names: Overview is Home, Analytics is Usage at `/usage` and Operations is Services at `/services`.
migrations.instructions: The release renamed them with no redirect, and an update writes none of the team's pages, views or tests. Each file listed is one of them or names one: a page or a view, the view tools, `src/app.config.ts`'s nav and the feature ids it names, the routes of `scripts/verify.config.ts`, or a shipped test that expects them. A project that kept the sample's pages as they were brings the release's over: `app/(dashboard)/` and `app/embed/`, `src/views/`, `src/data/`, `src/lib/assistant/` beside `prompt.ts`, `src/app.config.ts` with its own `app` kept, and each shipped test as the release has it; a file listed here that the release no longer has is deleted. A project that made the pages its own keeps its own names, makes the changes this release's other migrations list in them, and reads "not applicable" for the assistant walk-through's steps on Home and Now (`scripts/lib/sample.ts`).
